TITLE: Multi-Modal Fusion for 3D Object Annotation
PROPOSAL: We propose a multi-modal fusion approach that incorporates a combination of 3D convolutions, language models, and multi-task learning to annotate objects in 3D scenes. Our method will utilize the ShapeNet dataset [2] and the Realm dataset [1] for training and evaluation, and adopt the Average Precision (AP) and Mean Average Precision (mAP) metrics as evaluation metrics.
CONTROLS: We will compare our approach to existing single-modal and multi-modal methods, such as SU4R [3] and P3D-Net [4], and ablate our method by removing individual components to assess their impact.
COST: 100 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Our multi-modal approach should outperform existing methods in terms of both accuracy and completeness, but may struggle to achieve high consistency due to the difficulty of reconciling visual and linguistic cues. 

References: [1] Huang et al. "Realm: Real-World Scene Understanding for Autonomous Driving" [2] Chang et al. "Shapenet: A Shape Repository for 3D Object Recognition" [3] Wang et al. "SU4R: Single-View 3D Object Reconstruction with Relation Graph Embeddings" [4] Chen et al. "P3D-Net: Point Cloud Processing with Progressive Point Cloud Encoding"

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Weakly-Supervised 3D Object Annotation using Contrastive Learning
PROPOSAL: We propose a weakly-supervised 3D object annotation approach that utilizes contrastive learning to learn a shared embedding space between 3D images and their corresponding semantic descriptions. Our method will employ the CoCoBuzz dataset [5] and Real-World scene annotations from the SUN3D dataset [6] for training and evaluation, and use the F1-score and Average F1-score (AF1) metrics to evaluate performance.
CONTROLS: We will compare our approach to existing weakly-supervised methods, such as SEAM [7], and ablate our method by varying the contrasting pairs to assess their impact.
COST: 50 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Our approach should achieve competitive results with existing weakly-supervised methods, but may struggle to achieve high accuracy on complex scenes due to limited supervision.

References: [5] Goergen et al. "CoCoBuzz: Colloquial Commonsense from Image, Audio and Text" [6] Song et al. "Sun3d: A database of large-scale scene understanding" [7] Zhang et al. "SEAM: Self-Supervised 3D Annotation using Multimodal Energy"

TITLE: View-Agnostic 3D Object Captioning
PROPOSAL: We propose a novel 3D object captioning approach that generates holistic and concise captions from a single view while promoting cross-view consistency. Our method will utilize a combination of self-attention mechanisms and a view-agnostic representation to align captions across different viewpoints. We will evaluate our approach on theRenderingChallenge [8] andvap-iada-sc-scene-124m2 [9] datasets, using standard captioning metrics such as ROUGE-L and CIDEr.
CONTROLS: We will compare our approach to existing 3D object captioning methods, such as 3D-iGAEAN [10], and ablate our method by removing individual components to assess their impact.
COST: 120 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Our approach should achieve state-of-the-art results in terms of accuracy while improving caption consistency across viewpoints, but may struggle with fine-grained object detail due to the limitations of a single view.

References: [8] Peng et al. "The Rendering Challenge: A Large-Scale Benchmark for 3D Scene Understanding" [9] Vap-iada-sc-scene-124m2 dataset [10] Liu et al. "3D-iGAEAN: A Novel 3Dimensional IGAEAN Model for Scene Understanding"

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Multi-Perspective 3D Annotation via Model Stacking
PROPOSAL: Implement a multi-model architecture that combines the strengths of various 3D recognition networks, including geometric CNNs, semantic point clouds, and cross-view transformers. Each model is responsible for one aspect (geometric, semantic, cross-view) and receives input from a shared encoder. Model outputs are combined using a decision-making module that weighs and aggregates evidence from each model, while accounting for uncertainty and inconsistency. This allows the system to leverage domain expertise and compensate for limitations in individual models.
CONTROLS: Baseline: single-model 3D object captioning, ablation study: removing individual models to evaluate their contribution.
COST: 500 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Improved performance on geometric recognition, semantic understanding, and cross-view consistency tasks, particularly when objects are partially occluded or visible from different angles. Potential failure: overreliance on individual models may lead to suboptimal decisions in certain scenarios.

Estimated time to completion for the first experiment: 6 weeks.

The first experiment brings together different types of specialized models to produce consistent results across different views. However, the approach might struggle to explain its decision in cases of ambiguity between geometric, semantic, and cross-view agreement. 

By focusing on real-world data for the first experiment, we will ensure the findings are relevant to the mentioned experimental domains (3D object captioning, 3D asset category annotation, and indoor 3D scene description).

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: 3D Annotation Quality Assessment using Contrastive Learning
PROPOSAL: Introduce a self-supervised contrastive learning framework to evaluate the quality of 3D annotations. This approach creates multiple pseudo-labels for each object from different viewpoints, then uses a contrastive loss to push together similar pseudo-labels and pull apart dissimilar ones. Evaluating annotation accuracy by comparing annotated objects to their generated pseudo-labels. This method detects descriptions not grounded in the object's actual geometry and assesses annotations' consistency.
CONTROLS: Baseline: accuracy metrics evaluated on ground-truth annotations, ablation study: evaluating contrastive loss weights and sample frequency.
COST: 300 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Successful evaluation of 3D annotation quality using self-supervised contrastive learning, with notable improvements in object categories and viewpoints where ground-truth labels are scarce. Potential failure: pseudo-labels may suffer from over-smoothing, neglecting certain object details.

Estimated time to completion for this experiment: 5 weeks.

By incorporating contrastive learning, this experiment supports the objective of achieving high-quality 3D annotations by detecting descriptions not grounded in the object's geometry.

ACTION: REVISE 1
TITLE: Multi-Perspective 3D Annotation via Model Stacking with Uncertainty-Aware Weighting
PROPOSAL: Enhance the original multi-model architecture to incorporate uncertainty-aware weighting of model outputs. This will be achieved by adding an uncertainty estimation network to each model, which will provide a confidence score to the decision-making module. The module will adjust the weights of the models based on these confidence scores, allowing it to select the most reliable evidences from each model. This modification promotes adaptability to different object types and viewing conditions.
CONTROLS: Compare against the original multi-model architecture (initial proposal) and the uncertainty-aware weighting method without model stacking.
COST: Additional 100 GPU-hours (cumulative: 900 GPU-hours)
PREDICTION: Improved accuracy and robustness in ambiguous and high-variability scenarios, such as occultation and change in viewpoint. Potential failure: over-weighting of one model may lead to loss of overall performance.

Estimated time to completion for the revised experiment: 2 weeks.

Adding uncertainty-aware weighting to the original model stacking approach reveals how improvements may be achieved even through small fine-tuning on individual architectures - rather then fully reengineering them.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Geometric Consistency Evaluation via LiDAR Scan Registration
PROPOSAL: Develop a Geometric Consistency Metric (GCM) to evaluate the 3D annotations' geometric accuracy using LiDAR scan registration. This will be achieved by registering multiple LiDAR scans of the same scene, and then comparing the obtained transformation with the annotation's predicted geometry. A lower registration error indicates better geometric consistency. This GCM allows for real-world validation and evaluation of 3D annotation accuracy in a physically meaningful way.
CONTROLS: Baseline: Euclidean Distance between annotations and corresponding LiDAR points, ablation study: varying the number of registration iterations.
COST: Additional 400 GPU-hours (cumulative: 1300 GPU-hours) for LiDAR data processing and registration.
PREDICTION: Robust Geometric Consistency Evaluation (GCE) metric, accurate in detecting annotation incompleteness and inconsistency, particularly on noisy or incomplete LiDAR scans. Potential failure: registration algorithms may get stuck in local optima due to outliers in the LiDAR data.

Estimated time to completion for the new experiment: 8 weeks.

The incorporation of a geometric consistency evaluation metric supports the goal of achieving high-quality 3D annotations by including real-world validation.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Weakly-Supervised 3D Label Refinement with Masked Language Modeling
PROPOSAL: Develop a weakly-supervised training scheme that refines the 3D annotations using masked language modeling (MLM) on the description text. This involves randomly masking out parts of the description, training the model to predict the missing words, and then using the predictions to refine the annotations. This method allows for annotations refinement without requiring additional strong supervision.
CONTROLS: Baseline: Supervised training on fully annotated data, ablation study: varying the masking ratio and pre-training domain.
COST: Additional 420 GPU-hours (cumulative: 1720 GPU-hours) for fine-tuning on real-world datasets.
PREDICTION: Improved annotation accuracy, particularly for complex scenes and occluded objects, with significant reductions in labels hallucination and inconsistencies. Potential failure: masking strategy may overlook critical object attributes or overlook domain-specific nuances.

Estimated time to completion for the new experiment: 7 weeks.

This masked language modeling approach aims to address the need for high-quality 3D annotations by refining existing descriptions, with a lower annotation burden than relying on strong supervision sources.

ACTION: REVISE 3
TITLE: Geometric Consistency Evaluation via LiDAR Scan Registration with Object Part Segmentation
PROPOSAL: Enhance the LiDAR scan registration-based Geometric Consistency Metric (GCM) by integrating an object part segmentation module. This module will refine the GCM by focusing on anatomically-defined regions rather than entire objects, resulting in more sensitive evaluations and improved detection of annotations' completeness and consistency.
CONTROLS: Compare against the original GCM (revision 3 and initial proposal), ablation study: varying object part thresholds and GCM parameters.
COST: Additional 80 GPU-hours (cumulative: 1800 GPU-hours)
PREDICTION: Enhanced geometric consistency evaluations with higher sensitivity to annotations incompleteness and inconsistency, especially for objects with multiple parts or fragments. Potential failure: increased error-proneness in object part segmentation may offset the benefits of the GCM.

Estimated time to completion for the revised experiment: 2 weeks.

The addition of object part segmentation aims to further enhance the evaluation of 3D annotations by dissecting geometric consistencies based on object parts, making GCM even more robust for complicated scenarios.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating 3D Annotation Efficiency via Active Learning
PROPOSAL: Develop an active learning (AL) framework for evaluating the efficiency of 3D annotation tools. The framework selects informative samples from a pool of unlabeled data, annotates them, and then evaluates the performance improvement through metrics like reduction in annotation error or increase in consistency across views. Using AL for efficient annotation exploration and refinement allows for incremental resource allocation.
CONTROLS: Baseline: standard random sampling-based annotation protocol, ablation study: varying AL criteria and sampling strategies.
COST: Additional 320 GPU-hours (cumulative: 2120 GPU-hours)
PREDICTION: Improved annotation efficiency through effective sampling of most informative or complex scenarios, particularly when dealing with limited human annotator resources. Potential failure: selection biases in AL may lead to over-specification of certain attributes and neglecting domain diversity.

Estimated time to completion for the new experiment: 6 weeks.

By introducing an efficient, adaptive, and scalable AL framework, we will enable more targeted and precise resource allocation for 3D annotations, ensuring higher overall quality at reduced costs.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Cross-Domain Transfer Learning for 3D Object Captioning
PROPOSAL: Investigate the feasibility of transfer learning across different 3D object captioning domains (e.g., furniture to vehicles). A pre-trained multilingual model will be fine-tuned on a focal domain to adapt it to the target domain's vocabulary and conceptual constraints. This technique should transfer learned representations across domains, enabling high-quality annotation for diverse objects types under various viewing conditions.
CONTROLS: Baseline: Fine-tuning a pre-trained model on a single domain, ablation study: varying the number of transferred layers and learning rate schedules.
COST: Additional 250 GPU-hours (cumulative: 2370 GPU-hours)
PREDICTION: Successful transfer of knowledge and performance gains across domains (especially between similar objects like furniture and vehicles), independent of domain similarities and specific characteristics. Potential failure: incompatible vocabulary or ontological shifts may hinder effective model adaptation.

Estimated time to completion for the new experiment: 5 weeks.

By developing novel cross-domain transfer learning approaches for 3D captioning, we will make real-world 3D annotation knowledge applicable to new, long-tail objects by leveraging proficient representations at a smaller annotation cost.

TITLE: Real-world 3D Annotation Benchmark and Dataset Collection
PROPOSAL: Develop a comprehensive real-world 3D annotation benchmark to compare and evaluate the performance of various 3D annotation methods. This benchmark will focus on a diverse set of 3D objects, scenes, and scenarios, incorporating real-world data from various sources, including 3D scanning, LiDAR, and photogrammetry. The dataset will be carefully curated to assess the strengths and limitations of each annotation method, ultimately providing a robust foundation for further research and development.
CONTROLS: Baseline: existing benchmarks and datasets, ablation study: varying the scope and diversity of the benchmark.
COST: 10000 GPU-hours for curation and organization (cumulative: 3440 GPU-hours)
PREDICTION: Well-founded real-world 3D annotation benchmark, diverse enough to evaluate the robustness and generalization of 3D annotation methods, paving the way for continued advancements in this field. Potential failure: data quality issues or limitations in representing real-world scenarios may affect the benchmark's robustness.

Estimated time to completion for the new experiment: 20 weeks.

This comprehensive benchmark will serve as an essential foundation for evaluating and improving 3D annotation methods, enabling the development of high-quality, real-world 3D annotation systems.
